references.text: Noah's curse on Canaan, where he was to be a 'slave of slaves' for his brothers, a parallel to the Gibeonites' fate as servants.
Moses mentions 'the one who chops your wood and the one who draws your water' as part of the covenant assembly, the same tasks assigned to the Gibeonites.
Earlier in the same chapter, the Gibeonites are appointed to be woodcutters and water carriers for the entire congregation.
Joshua carries out the judgment and makes the Gibeonites woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and for the altar of the Lord.
The Gibeonites are mentioned again during David's time, where Saul's treatment of them has consequences for Israel.
The 'Nethinim' (temple slaves) who returned from exile are believed to descend from the Gibeonites who were given to sanctuary service.
